ai.description: This slender, arboreal snake reaches 1 meter. It is bronze-brown dorsally with a distinct black lateral stripe and a yellow venter. Key features include a prominent eye stripe and a bluish neck patch.
ai.identificationRemarks: Dendrelaphis humayuni is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, thin black line running along the center of the vertebral scale row, which is absent in similar species.
ai.habitat: Dendrelaphis humayuni inhabits the moist deciduous and semi-evergreen forests of the Western Ghats, typically found in mid-to-high altitude hill ranges.
ai.behavior: Dendrelaphis humayuni is a diurnal, arboreal snake that actively hunts for small lizards and frogs among tree branches and foliage.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Dendrelaphis humayuni* is oviparous, laying clutches of 3–5 eggs. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season in India.
ai.distributionRemarks: Dendrelaphis humayuni is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, primarily occurring in the states of Maharashtra, Goa, and Karnataka at mid-to-high elevations.
